pigments.name: Azurite
pigments.title: Azurite
pigments.description:
**Chemical Formula**
Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2
**Period of use in Art**
Known since the 25th century BC and used until 1800.
Description
Azurite is a rather rare and precious pigment obtained by grinding the copper mineral of the same name. Its use has been documented since the third millennium BC, and it was used as early as the Fourth Egyptian Dynasty, although it was not widely used at the time due to its instability. In Roman times, it was described by Pliny under the name Lapis Armenium. In the Middle Ages, azurite gained importance and was used extensively.
The pigment is a basic copper carbonate, unstable and reactive, which when in contact with lime and when heated, turns into black copper oxide (tenorite, CuO), so it is not recommended for use in fresco techniques. Even when applied dry, it can cause problems as it undergoes degradation due to humidity, chloride attack, and the presence of sulfides, which lead to the formation of copper sulfide and therefore to darkening of the color.
Azurite is associated with another copper-based pigment, malachite, which is green in color. Azurite and Malachite share the same chemical nature but with a different crystal structure. When azurite is exposed to air and humid conditions, the process of transformation into malachite can be activated thanks to this reaction: 
2[2CuCO3⋅Cu(OH)2] + H2O→3 [CuCO3⋅Cu(OH)2] + CO2
Microscopically, the alteration is often observed as a green malachite overgrowth or pseudomorphic replacement on azurite particles, leading to a gradual chromatic shift from blue to green. This phenomenon is particularly relevant in wall paintings and polychrome artworks, where it represents a key degradation pathway affecting original color appearance.

instruments.FORS:
**FORS** (Fiber Optic Reflectance Spectroscopy)
Provides reflectance vs wavelength in the _visible/near-infrared_ range.
instruments.FT-IR:
**FT-IR** (Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy)
Measures _absorption_ in the _mid-infrared_ (wavenumber) region.
instruments.Raman:
**Raman spectroscopy**
Provides _vibrational spectra_ useful for identifying molecular species.
